newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end sharply lower in nervous trade.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end sharply lower in nervous trade.

text.p: Blue chips skidded to sharp losses on Monday, as political fears clouded market sentiment after a regional party said it plans to pull out of the ruling United Front minority government, traders said.
"People tend to discount political news, but when it comes in reality, markets take a fall like this," said Ashith Kampani, head of dealing at JM Share & Stock Brokers.

Despite the sell-off, the market could see an upward charge as the government faced no immediate threat, traders said. The 30-share Bombay index was off 98.37 points, or 2.3 percent, at 4,223.61, its biggest fall since a 303-point tumble on March 30.
"The market was in an overbought position and bull liquidation pulled down prices," said Kamal Kabra, a member-broker of the Bombay Stock Exchange.
A nominal fall in the Bombay index forced stocks to close in negative territory last week -- the first time since May 23.

Tobacco giant ITC figured among the major losers, tumbling 36.0 rupees to 507.50 on Monday after the government launched an enquiry into the firm's alleged violations of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA), traders said.
The federal Enforcement Directorate is investigating in the $110 million FERA violation case, local newspapers said.

The market will now take cue from new political developments, traders said. The DMK party of Industry Minister Murasoli Maran said in a statement it planned to pull out of Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral's 15-party government but would continue to provide support from the outside.
DMK leaders blamed the Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M), accusing it of interfering in Gujral's Janata Dal party.
The DMK accounts for less than a tenth in the United Front's 178 seats in the 545-member lower house of parliament.
